evidence_tree.build_command: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

sources_quoted.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
sources_quoted.derived: C = 5 max stacks; per-stack reduction = 6%; cap = 30% armor reduction; stack duration = 6 s, refreshed by every physical damage instance.

sources_quoted.quote: Dealing physical damage to champions reduces the target's Armor by 6% for 6 seconds. (stacks 5 times).
sources_quoted.derived: Corroborates 6% x 5 = 30% from the game-client string, independent of the wiki prose branch.

sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).
sources_quoted.derived: Expose Weakness is a flat multiplicative amp (8% melee / 5% ranged, {{rd|melee|ranged}} convention confirmed against 40+ other {{rd|..}} usages in the same cache). Being a common multiplicative factor on the whole breakdown row, it CANCELS in the old/new ratio and cannot by itself explain the observed delta (see rejected_hypotheses).

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 2.3 item 2 ('Black Cleaver average stacks')
sources_quoted.quote: the established model uses a fixed `0.8*max_stacks` constant (with a `hits/2` short-fight branch). Under the engine's own ordering convention (4 leading ability hits apply stacks before the auto stream) the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp `min(k, C)` over `h` hits is `C - C(C-1)/(2h)` for `h >= C`; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes. The stack *duration* (6 s) is always longer than the engine's inter-swing interval for any realistic AS*u > 1/6, so expiry does not rescue the constant - this is a documented tuning constant, not a theorem.
sources_quoted.derived: 0.8 * C = 0.8 * 5 = 4.0 stacks = 24% reduction is the OLD model. It is exact only at h = 10 hits and is biased LOW for every longer fight. The doc itself labels it APPROX and recommends replacing it with the closed form.
Mitigation multiplier used for every arithmetic step below.

sources_quoted.quote: R_final = max(0, (R - r_flat)*(1 - r_pct/100)*(1 - p) - f)
sources_quoted.derived: Composition order: Carve's percentage reduction applies to armor BEFORE penetration; flat pen subtracts last, floored at 0.

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 2.3 preamble + row 'Terminus/BC ramps' of the Section 5 audit table
sources_quoted.quote: m(R) convex => averaging understates ramp damage (Jensen); BC constant = exact mean at ~10 autos, +/-20% at extremes
sources_quoted.derived: Any averaged-stack model is a LOWER bound on the true per-hit ramp sum; the exact per-hit simulation is strictly larger.

independent_computation.step_1_source_rule: Carve per-hit armor-reduction sequence for a participant landing h physical damage instances: r_k = 6% * min(k, 5), capped at 30%. Correct damage total = SUM_k raw_k * m(A_k), never a single constant.

step_2_stack_means.formula: mean stacks over h hits = C - C(C-1)/(2h) with C = 5  =>  5 - 10/h
step_2_stack_means.conclusion: The old model's 4.0 stacks / 24% is the exact ramp mean at exactly h = 10 physical hits. A coupled roster fight with a Black Cleaver carrier (4 leading ability hits + a sustained auto stream, 6 s stack duration never lapsing) has h >> 10, so the source rule REQUIRES a mean strictly above 24% and the change's direction (upward) is forced.

step_3_observed_delta.interpretation: Expose Weakness (8%/5%) and every non-armor factor are common multiplicative factors on this row and cancel in the ratio, so the ratio isolates the change in the physical-damage mitigation multiplier m(A_eff).

step_4_solve_for_the_reduction.identity: ratio = m(A_eff_new) / m(A_eff_old) = (100 + A*(1-r_old)*(1-p) - f) / (100 + A*(1-r_new)*(1-p) - f)
step_4_solve_for_the_reduction.method: Exhaustive grid over integer target armor A in [20,260], flat pen f in [0,40], percent pen p in {0,.10,.15,.18,.20,.24,.25,.30,.35,.40,.45}, holding r_old = 24%.
step_4_solve_for_the_reduction.result: 1386 parameterisations reproduce ratio = 1.03478 to within 3e-4 with r_new = 30% (the wiki cap). Best fits include (A=79, f=19, p=0), (A=113, f=5, p=18%), (A=101, f=12, p=15%), (A=131, f=6, p=30%) - all ordinary level-18/20 armor and lethality values. Cesaro-mean values of r_new (27%-29.4%) also fit, at correspondingly higher armor. No parameterisation reproduces the ratio with r_new <= 24%: the observed change is only reachable by increasing Carve's effective reduction toward the 30% cap.

worked_example.assumed: target armor A = 79, attacker flat armor pen (lethality) f = 19, percent pen p = 0

exact_per_hit_ramp.note: computed as old * (mean_k m(A_k)) / m(0.76A) with A_k = 79*(1 - 0.06*min(k,5)) - 19

step_5_verdict_logic.old_value: 3226.1 corresponds to a flat 24% Carve reduction, i.e. exactly 0.8 * 5 stacks. This is the tuning constant that docs/math-foundations.md Section 2.3 labels 'a documented tuning constant, not a theorem', exact only at h = 10 hits. For a sustained coupled roster fight it is outside the band the wiki rule permits and biased low. REJECTED.
step_5_verdict_logic.new_value: 3338.3 lies inside the band the wiki rule permits: [exact-per-hit-ramp, 30% cap]. Under the best-fitting realistic parameterisation it reproduces the 30% five-stack cap to 0.01 damage (3338.29 vs 3338.3); under higher-armor parameterisations it reproduces the exact Cesaro/per-hit ramp. Either reading is source-consistent. ACCEPTED.
step_5_verdict_logic.both_wrong_test: 'both_wrong' would require the new value to exceed the ceiling the source permits. The ceiling is the 30% five-stack cap; the observed delta is reachable at or below that cap for many ordinary armor/penetration values, so the new value is not provably over-stated. Not selected.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Expose Weakness corrected from the ranged 5% to the melee 8%
Expose Weakness newly applied at 8% across the whole row
Expose Weakness newly applied at 8% over only part of the window
rejected_hypotheses.result: rejected as unmotivated; with a 10 s spellblade window and a 1.5 s cooldown the 4 s debuff is near-permanent in a sustained fight, so neither fraction has a source basis

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Bloodsong Spellblade proc count off by one (100% base AD bonus physical)
rejected_hypotheses.test: delta 112.2 would be one post-mitigation proc; requires ~180 base AD at ~40 effective armor
rejected_hypotheses.result: rejected; no champion in data/champions.json reaches that base AD at the level cap, and the hypothesis leaves the Carve constant unexplained

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Penetration/reduction ORDER bug (pen applied before Carve's percentage reduction)
rejected_hypotheses.test: the two orderings differ by exactly f*r_pct of armor; with f = 19 and r = 0.30 that is 5.7 armor, which also lands in range
rejected_hypotheses.result: not excluded, but it is the SAME correction in substance - both readings move the effective post-Carve armor down by the amount the wiki-quoted composition order (Section 2.2) demands, and both push the leaf upward. Verdict is unchanged.

residual_uncertainty: The scenario definition for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' (champions, levels, items, target, fight window) lives outside the permitted evidence tree - it is not in data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json nor anywhere else under data/. The absolute leaf value therefore cannot be reconstructed from first principles; the computation above pins the RATIO, which is exactly where the change lives, and bounds it against the wiki-sourced band.

Within that band I cannot distinguish 'engine now holds max 5 stacks (30%)' from 'engine now uses the exact Cesaro/per-hit ramp'. If the former, the new value still over-states the first 4 hits of the ramp by a bounded amount (0.3-1.6% for h = 100 down to h = 20 in the worked parameterisation) - materially closer to the source rule than the old 24% constant, but not the exact ramp. That is a follow-up worth checking against the scenario's actual hit count, not grounds to call the new value wrong.
conclusion: The League Wiki cache (data/items.json 3071 Carve: 6% per stack, 5 stacks, 30% cap, 6 s) combined with the closed form quoted in docs/math-foundations.md Section 2.3 (mean stacks = C - C(C-1)/(2h) = 5 - 10/h) shows that the old leaf is pinned to a flat 4-stack / 24% tuning constant that is correct only for a 10-hit fight and biased low for every longer one. The observed +3.4779% move is reproducible to 0.01 damage by raising Carve's effective reduction to the wiki-sourced 30% five-stack cap under ordinary armor and lethality values, and is unreachable at any reduction <= 24%. The new value is the source-consistent one.
